newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BLEWETT OUT FOR 99 AS AUSTRALIA SLOWS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BLEWETT OUT FOR 99 AS AUSTRALIA SLOWS.

text.p: An expectant Adelaide Oval crowd was stunned into silence on Monday when home town boy Greg Blewett was bowled for 99 in the morning session of the third day of Australia's fourth test against the West Indies.
Australia lost three wickets and scored just 60 runs in 26 overs to be 494 for eight at lunch, their lowest scoring session of the match.

A careful Blewett seemed to be forging inexorably towards his third century when right arm fast-bowler Cameron Cuffy sent down a ball that seamed back between Blewett's bat and pad to clip the top of off-stump.
The 25-year-old South Australian strode from a hushed ground in disbelief, his head down and cursing.
The crowd of about 20,000 only just managed to stir itself and summon a standing ovation as Blewett walked into the dressing room.
One of the few left sitting in the stands was Blewett's girlfriend, who was slumped with her head in her hands.
Blewett scored his maiden test century on his debut against England on this same ground in 1995 to the acclaim of his fellow South Australians.
Australia's attempt to build a huge lead over the West Indies' paltry first-innings total of 130 resumed quietly at 434 for five and was virtually stopped in its tracks with Blewett's dismissal.
A strangely hesitant Michael Bevan poked and prodded his way to 71 not out at lunch, adding just 24 runs in the session.
The West Indies' young fast bowlers, Cuffy and Patterson Thompson, finally found a good line and length in the morning session.

Each took a wicket, with Cuffy's ball to dismiss Blewett as good as any in the match. The West Indies attack was depleted on the morning of the first day when strike fast-bowler Curtly Ambrose, the main destroyer in the West Indies third test match victory, withdrew with a groin injury.
Australia's stranglehold on the match remains tight however, having built a lead of 364 by lunch with eight sessions to play.

Australia, who lead the best of five match series 2-1, are still virtually assured of at least a draw, which would be enough for the hosts to retain the Frank Worrell trophy they won in the Caribbean in 1995.
